summary: Iteration 2 re-test of the main agent's fixes. Backend: cleared stale login_attempts, re-ran the existing 52-test suite (all 52 now pass, incl. the 4 previously failing tests: GET /api/ health, brute-force, tech-cannot-PATCH-equipment, tech-cannot-DELETE-failure) and added a new 13-test file /app/backend/tests/test_site_scope.py covering the full site-scope matrix on every mutating single-doc route (equipments/parts/failures/analyses/maintenance PATCH+DELETE+complete), site reassignment via PATCH payload, health payload, brute-force lockout, stock-movements part_id filter preservation and cascade deletes. 65 tests total; 64 pass deterministically. The ONLY remaining backend defect is the brute-force lockout key: it is keyed on request.client.host which behind the k8s ingress is the ingress POD ip (observed .137 and .138), so failed attempts are split across pods and the 6th attempt is usually still 401 (lockout only triggers after ~9-12 attempts, non-deterministically). Frontend smoke: login page no longer prints any demo credentials, 'Pannes par type' now has 2 Y axes and both series render with visible height (202px vs 60px), Sonner toaster mounts bottom-right (y=bottom, x=right; toast rect top=1002 vs header bottom=61 - header no longer covered), tech role can navigate all 5 pages and legitimately create/save on its own site (toast 'Enregistré'), no console errors. All test data created was removed; DB back to seed baseline (2 sites, 5 equipments, 5 parts, 3 failures, 5 analyses, 1 maintenance task, 3 users).

minor.issue: Lockout counter key is f'{request.client.host}:{email}' but request.client.host is the ingress pod IP, not the caller. Observed two distinct keys per email (10.231.129.137 / .138), so 5 real failures produce only 2-3 per key => 6th attempt returns 401. Live probe of 14 sequential wrong passwords: [401 x8, 423,423,423, 401, 423,423]. tests/test_site_scope.py::TestBruteForce::test_lockout_on_sixth_attempt fails 3/3 in isolation (passed once in a full parallel run => flaky). Fix: key on email only (optionally + first IP of X-Forwarded-For) and/or store attempts on the user document.

12 orphan stock_movements and 3 orphan maintenance_history rows created BEFORE the cascade fix are still in the DB (new cascade works: verified 0 orphans after DELETE /api/parts/{id} and DELETE /api/maintenance/{id}). Consider a one-off cleanup.
Still CORS_ORIGINS="*" in backend/.env with allow_credentials=True (unchanged from iteration 1; playbook asks for explicit origins).
Unchanged from iteration 1: editing parts_used does not reconcile stock movements (stock desync on edit).

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force RCA: db.login_attempts documents are keyed by `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"`. In this Kubernetes preview the FastAPI app sees the ingress pod address as client host, and requests round-robin between at least two pods (10.231.129.137 / 10.231.129.138). Each pod therefore accumulates its own counter, so N failed attempts become ~N/2 per key and the documented '6th attempt => 423' behaviour does not hold (reproduced: 6 attempts => all 401; 14 attempts => first 423 on attempt 9). Additionally, since the real client IP is never used, the counter is effectively global-per-email once XFF is honoured - so the simplest correct fix is to key by email only (with a TTL/unlock cleanup), or parse X-Forwarded-For[0] if per-IP throttling is desired.
